title: Yash's 'Toxic' Trailer Set for Grand Bengaluru Unveiling on August 8
excerpt: The makers of India's most expensive Kannada film will launch the trailer at a large-scale event in Karnataka's capital, weeks before the period gangster drama hits theatres worldwide on August 26.
body:
• The official trailer for Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups will be unveiled at a grand event in Bengaluru on August 8, exactly two years after shooting began
  • The period gangster film, directed by Geetu Mohandas and budgeted at ₹600 crore, releases worldwide on August 26 coinciding with Onam — in IMAX, Dolby Cinema, 4DX and D-Box formats
  • Distribution deals already total over ₹348 crore across domestic and overseas markets, making Toxic one of the most commercially ambitious Indian films in history

The countdown to one of Indian cinema's biggest releases of 2026 enters its final phase next week. The makers of Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups have confirmed that the film's official trailer will launch on August 8 at a large-scale event in Bengaluru, according to multiple industry reports. The trailer reveal comes just 18 days before the film's worldwide theatrical release on August 26.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=j1XGlaEqCls

The date carries symbolic weight. August 8 marks exactly two years since principal photography commenced in Bengaluru with a traditional pooja ceremony in 2024. For Yash — the KGF franchise star who hasn't appeared on screen in over four years — the trailer represents the most anticipated reveal in a promotional campaign that has already generated extraordinary numbers.

A Calculated Promotional Buildup

The road to the trailer has been carefully staged. A character glimpse titled "Introducing Raya," released on January 8 to coincide with Yash's 40th birthday, amassed over 200 million views and 5.5 million likes within 24 hours across platforms. An official teaser followed on February 20, and a second promotional clip titled "Ladies & Ladies" arrived on July 1, offering the first proper look at the film's ensemble female cast — Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria and Rukmini Vasanth.

Bengaluru was always the intended venue for the trailer launch. When Toxic was initially slated for a March 2026 release, the team had planned a similar event in the city. Those plans were shelved after the release date was postponed — one of several delays that pushed the film from its original April 2025 window through March and June 2026 dates before landing on August 26.

"Co-writing Toxic with Yash has been a privilege and a thrill."

— Geetu Mohandas, Director

Scale and Stakes

Directed by Geetu Mohandas — known for critically acclaimed work on Moothon and Liar's Dice — Toxic pairs an auteur sensibility with blockbuster scale. The period gangster drama features Yash in a dual role as characters named Raya and Rumi (also known as Ticket), and was shot simultaneously in Kannada and English across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Goa, Thoothukudi and Jaipur over a 14-month production schedule.

The technical team reflects the film's global ambitions. Hollywood stunt choreographer JJ Perry designed the action sequences alongside Indian duo Anbariv. Acclaimed cinematographer Rajeev Ravi handled the visuals, while DNEG — the VFX studio behind multiple Hollywood tentpoles — delivered the visual effects. Ravi Basrur, who composed the iconic KGF scores, returns for the background music.

The commercial stakes are equally massive. Distribution deals already announced include ₹180 crore for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (acquired by Sri Venkateswara Film Distributors), ₹105 crore for overseas markets (Phars Film), and ₹63 crore for Tamil Nadu — collectively exceeding ₹348 crore before a single ticket is sold. The film will release in six languages: Kannada, English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam, across IMAX, Dolby Cinema, 4DX and D-Box formats.

The Global Audience

Toxic's marketing has deliberately targeted audiences beyond India's borders. The film has already topped IMDb's Most Anticipated Indian Movies and Shows list, and its pan-Indian cast — spanning Kannada, Hindi, Tamil and Malayalam cinema — is designed to draw audiences across linguistic markets. The Onam release window, coinciding with one of South India's major festivals, adds built-in audience momentum in Kerala and among the global Malayali diaspora.

For Indian cinema audiences overseas, Toxic represents a test case for whether a Kannada-origin film can replicate the KGF franchise's crossover success on an even larger scale. KGF: Chapter 2 grossed over ₹1,200 crore worldwide in 2022, establishing Yash as one of the few South Indian stars with genuine pan-India and international drawing power.

What's Next

The August 8 trailer event is expected to bring together the cast and crew alongside fans and media in Bengaluru. Two songs — "Tabaahi" featuring Vishal Mishra and "Manamohaka" composed by Tanishk Bagchi — have already been released as part of the music rollout. With the trailer launch, the final promotional push begins in earnest ahead of what the industry is positioning as one of the defining releases of 2026.
nri_angle: Toxic tests whether a Kannada-origin film can match KGF's crossover box office success internationally, with its Onam release targeting diaspora audiences and overseas distribution rights already sold for ₹105 crore.
author: Diaspora Desk
